findings.note: A custom entry with a required core sensor's ID is checked only for required=true and retaining stages; it may replace the builtin/command and its options. For example, replacing required consistency with an always-successful command preserves those fields while removing the core check, so the overlay weakens a mandatory gate sensor.

Human-only answer enforcement trusts the caller-supplied actor string: _actor accepts --actor human:anything and _check_agent_actor does not authenticate that identity. An agent can invoke questions answer with a human-prefixed actor and mark an open question answered; the preToolUse guard does not block this command. This violates deterministic authorization and makes strict open-question checks bypassable.

profile_for errors are swallowed and strictness falls back to persisted depth only. If a basic-depth profile has guard_policy=strict and profile loading then fails (for example malformed/missing custom overlay), strict becomes false and the gate skips current-review and closed-question requirements rather than failing closed.

Only exact matching Q headers are parsed; other headings/records are silently ignored instead of raising a parse error. A small hand-edit/formatting deviation can make an unanswered question disappear from load_questions, causing both the questions sensor and strict gate check to report no open questions.
